title: Responses v4 compatibility: tool/function-calling + metadata routing + determinism flags
author: Maya Thompson
description: Add compatibility layer for Responses v4 semantics: structured/JSON output, first-class tool/function-calling surface, seed/determinism passthrough, and metadata routing for customer-provided fields. Motivation: customers adopting OpenAI's Responses variants were seeing mismatched streaming frames, dropped tool call tokens, and lost per-request metadata when proxied through Redwood. This PR implements a translation layer that preserves the v4 wire semantics while keeping Redwood's runtime guarantees (KV cache, streaming SLOs, and telemetry). Key behaviors: 1) Streaming reassembly adjusted to accept 'response.chunk' and 'response.delta' frames and re-emit Redwood streaming events with consistent chunk boundaries; 2) Tool/function-calling: map v4 function call objects to Redwood tool manifest entries and ensure function signature fidelity; allow early tool invocation (tool called mid-stream) and safe KV cache invalidation when a tool modifies context; 3) Determinism/seed passthrough: accept numerical seed and deterministic flags from client and surface to the sampler layer; preserve legacy Redwood sampler defaults when absent; 4) Metadata routing: copy request.metadata.* into route-level tags and ensure metadata_passthrough option is toggleable per-tenant; add audit log entries for all passthrough keys. Testing & rollout: feature gated behind a runtime flag resp_v4_compat. Unit + integration tests included; staged rollout to beta tenants before global enable. Checklist: - [x] end-to-end streaming tests - [x] function/tool call unit tests - [x] metadata preservation tests - [x] deterministic sampling tests - [x] add migration notes to API compatibility doc

ci_log_summary: Initial pipeline failed on lint and a streaming race test. Lint fixed by formatting SDK TS files; race test resolved by adding a small backoff in reassembly and increasing buffer capacity. Final run: all checks passed (unit, e2e, integration, lint, security-scan).
merge_outcome: Merged by squash-merge after approvals from Arjun and Sofia. Merge commit message: 'resp4: add v4 responses compatibility - tool calling, metadata passthrough, determinism flags'
release_notes: Beta: Responses v4 compatibility (feature-flagged). Supports structured JSON output, function/tool calling parity, seed/determinism passthrough, and metadata routing. Enable via tenant feature 'resp_v4_compat'.
notes_for_operators: Feature is behind runtime flag resp_v4_compat. Staged rollout recommended: enable for internal beta tenants, monitor metrics: streaming.reassembly.errors, tooling.invocation.latency, sampler.determinism. Audit logs for metadata_passthrough appear under audit.responses.v4. If issues observed, disable flag and restart api-gateway pods.
migration_guide_snippet: Clients using OpenAI Responses v4 should: 1) switch to Redwood's openai_compat SDK adapters (sdk/ts/openai_compat.ts or sdk/python/openai_compat.py) which translate responses v4 calls by default when resp_v4_compat is enabled; 2) avoid relying on implicit metadata copying unless tenant feature is enabled; 3) set 'seed' and 'deterministic' explicitly if repeatability is required; 4) verify function signatures with /v1/tools/list endpoint before rolling out.
qa_summary: E2E tests validate: streaming stability under concurrency 50, mid-stream tool call + KV mutation, deterministic repeatability over 5 seeds, metadata passthrough whitelist enforcement. Manual QA: exercised with three beta tenants and one enterprise Dedicated cluster. No regressions observed in baseline text-generation flows.
additional_context: Related work: follow-up PR planned to expose resp_v4 telemetry in Console and add per-route fallback policies for function-call failures. Cross-ref ENG-5380 for rollout milestones and SUP-879 for a customer support case that motivated metadata routing.
attention: Ops and SDK teams (Sofia, Arjun) for rollout coordination and SDK deprecation notes. Support: flag controls documented to avoid accidental data leakage by metadata passthrough.
